6. It has also been stated that recently the plaintiffs came to know from the office of the defendant No. 3 that the defendant No. 2 had included the suit land in Khas Khatian No.1. They were also informed from the said office that the defendants are trying to lease out the suit land to the defendant No. 4. Thereafter, on 26-11-1997 the plaintiff No. 2 procured the certified copy of the RS Khatian and found in the said Khatian Krantee share recorded in the name of the plaintiff No. 1 and other shares recorded in the names of their vendors but at the end of column 2 of the said RS Khatian, present address of the recordees is written as "'11\D It 1-tm-A1 mod" The said RS Khatian was prepared and published wrongly. It is stated that at the time of preparation of the said RS Khatian, the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were minors and students and plaintiff No. 1 being less educated, and also for his blindness could not take steps, which resulted such wrong recording. It has also been stated that there is no reason to extinguish proprietary right of the plaintiffs in the suit land under section 92(1)(e) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, or to be treated the same as vested property. Wrong recording of present address in RS Khatian and Memo dated 7-7-1997 under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, issued by the defendant No. 2, claiming the suit land as khas, has clouded title of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs are constrained to institute the present suit. 

 7. The defendants No. 1 to 3 filed a joint written statement denying the materials allegations made in the plaint and contenting interlaid that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and barred by the principles of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel. Their further contentions are that the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land. The sale deeds are forged, created and not acted upon. It has been further contended that after SA recorded tenants abandoned the suit land, the same is treated as khas land under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Transfer of Khas land in any manner is illegal and void. As the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land, and suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 11. Mr Md Abdul Alim Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submitted that the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from the owners who acquired their right, title and interest therein through Judgment and decree dated 13-12-1958 in Partition Suit No. 12 of 1938 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla and entered into possession through Execution Case No. 55 of 1960. Said title holders of the suit land during possession executed and registered sale deeds in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs mutated Khatians in their names and regularly paying rents in the Tahsil Office and municipal taxes in the municipality which were accepted by the relevant offices without any objection. The learned Advocate also submitted that the trial Court erred in law in disbelieving the exhibits filed by the plaintiffs without any .cogent reason though 'no objection was raised by the defendants at the time of admission of those exhibits. In this regard, the learned Advocate referred to the 'case of Joynal Abedin vs Hafizur Rahman, reported in 13 BLD (AD) 150 = 44 DLR (AD) 162 and also the case of Abdullah vs Abdul Karim, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. The learned Advocate also submitted that it is admitted by the defendants that the suit property was never included in the census list and the government has never taken possession of the land and, as such, wrong recording of present address in the RS Khatian can not extinguish the proprietary right of the plaintiffs acquired by registered title deeds. In this regard he referred to the case of Bangladesh vs Md Shahjahan, reported in 20 BLD (AD) 166. He next submitted that the trial Court erred in law in discarding the registered sale deeds of Asgar Ali Miah executed and registered more than 30 days ago and thus violates the provisions of section 90 of the Evidence Act. In this regard, he referred to the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin Pk, reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 and also the case of Kamaruddin @ Fakira vs Anisur Rahman, report-ed in 1 BLC 102. He also submitted that since the defendant No. 2 issued Memo under section 92(1)(c) of the SAT Act, extinguishing the proprietary right in the suit land declaring the same as Khas land, onus lies on the defendants to prove that the original raiyats abandoned the suit land without making any arrangement for payment of rent as it falls due. In this regard, he referred to the case of Gita Rani vs Bangladesh, reported in 36 DLR (AD) 225. The learned Advocate also submitted that in discarding the sale deeds executed and. registered under Registration Act, 1908 the trial Court violates the provisions of section 68 of the Evidence Act. In this regard, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Md Rafiq vs Md Zahur Nasir, reported in 8 DLR (WP) Lahore 56. He further submitted that after purchasing the suit land, the plaintiffs established filling station by taking permission from the defendant No. 2 which is evident from 'Exhibit-6. With such submissions, the learned Advocate prays to allow the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed the by the trial Court. 

 26. The relevant RS Khatian was prepared in the year 1969 to 1970 and finally published in the year 1980 but the impugned Memo under section 92(1)(c) issued on 7-7-1997 by the respondent No. 2 extinguishing proprietary right in the suit land. We failed to understand how the trial Court observe, that the land was recorded khas in the said RS Khatian.
